page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine within the GPU Machines family designed for artificial intelligence and compute-intensive tasks. The host configuration provides 26 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz across 13 physical cores. The CPU architecture incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector extensions. Hardware acceleration is supplied by one NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU featuring 80 GB of dedicated VRAM. The system is provisioned with 234 GB of system RAM, maintaining a memory allocation of 9.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 804 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core and compression performance. The configuration achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2072.0 and single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 33.6 GB/sec, placing it in the top performance quartiles for integer and compression tests. Multi-core operations show expected scaling for a 26-vCPU topology, producing a Passmark CPU score of 35694.46 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14893.0. In language model inference evaluations, the server achieves 348.05 tokens per second during text generation using a 135M parameter model, ranking in the top tier. However, generation rates decrease to 23.8 tokens per second on a 7B model and 2.49 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model, reflecting memory bandwidth and capacity boundaries when running large-scale language models on a single GPU.

Cost efficiency is focused around workloads requiring high GPU memory capacity without the architectural overhead of a distributed multi-GPU configuration. The pairing of 80 GB Hopper VRAM with a dense 9:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and local NVMe storage provides balanced local throughput. The instance lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring private networking or additional addressing configurations. Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-1g is best suited for small-to-medium parameter deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, computer vision pipelines, and accelerated data processing.

It features 26 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, backed by 234 GB of system memory and 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Graphics acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data reflects strong single-core CPU throughput, top-tier text generation for small language models reaching 348.05 tokens per second, and standard multi-core scaling. Throughput diminishes with 70B parameter models, indicating suitability boundaries for very large parameter workloads on a single accelerator. The instance offers high memory density and fast local storage, making it suited for deep learning fine-tuning, inference pipelines, computer vision, and GPU-driven analytical workloads.
